subject: Opsly SDK: semver compatibility request + feature-gate hooks
messages:
From: Kai Nakamura <kai@opsly.co>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: integrations@opsly.co, Emma Li <emma@opsly.co>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SDK contract + semver guidance for our adapter

Hi Aisha,

Quick note from the Integrations team at Opsly. We're prepping a major release of our platform (v3.0) and are planning to ship an Opsly -> Redwood adapter in our official SDK. Before we finalize, we need two things from Redwood:

1) A short, written compatibility guarantee for your public SDK layer (what we should pin to) — specifically, what constitutes a breaking change vs feature addition for your SDK client. Opsly needs to know whether we can rely on semver minor bumps without code changes.

2) A small hook/API for a runtime feature-gate so we can enable an optional batching optimization in our adapter that toggles Redwood's "prefetch_cache" behavior per-connection. We want this as a graceful opt-in so the majority of our customers aren't affected immediately.

We can share a patch and integration spec; attaching a rough diff and a PDF with our proposed flow. Could you route this to the right engineering owner so we can align timeline (we're aiming to ship Opsly v3.0 in July).

Thanks,
Kai
Senior PM, Integrations
Opsly

Attachments: opsly-sdk-patch.diff (text/diff), opsly-integration-specs.pdf (pdf)

Hi Kai — thanks for the detailed note and attachments. Appreciate the early heads-up.

I'll loop in our SDK and partnerships leads to confirm the compatibility semantics and feasibility of a feature-gate. Tentatively: we treat public client surface changes as semver-major; non-breaking additions (new optional parameters, hooks) as minor. But I'll let Jonas confirm specifics around the runtime flag.

Can you confirm whether the feature-gate needs to be toggled via API at request time, or if a per-connection flag at initialization is sufficient? The difference affects implementation complexity.

I'll follow up with a proposed timeline by EOD.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SDK contract + semver guidance for our adapter

Thanks for the ping. Quick technical read:

- Semver: the public SDK (client bindings, call signatures) should follow semver. Adding an optional parameter or an init-time option is a minor change as long as existing constructors and methods keep the same behavior when the option is absent.

- Feature-gate: implementing a per-connection init flag (e.g., Client({prefetch_cache: true})) is straightforward and non-breaking. A request-time header would be more intrusive (adds branching per-request and testing overhead). Per-connection gives Opsly control and avoids wide blast radius.

- Implementation path: add an optional boolean to the client options and a server-side toggle that respects that flag. We'll also need a short compatibility test in our SDK CI to assert default behavior remains unchanged.

Timeline (realistic but tight):
  * Prototype + unit tests: 1 week (by 2028-06-22)
  * Internal review + canary release (npm/pypi + docker tag): 1 week (by 2028-06-29)
  * Partner integration test with Opsly + docs: 1 week (by 2028-07-06)

Risks: the server-side respecting the flag requires a small change in routing layer to pass the connection-level metadata to the runtime. I estimate ~2 dev days server-side and ~2 dev days SDK-language work (we should prioritize JS + Python).

I'll volunteer the SDK team to own the client change; we should confirm engineering capacity and list of languages.

-Jonas
Lead Software Engineer, SDKs
Redwood Inference

From: Kai Nakamura <kai@opsly.co>

Subject: Re: Request: SDK contract + semver guidance for our adapter

Thanks, Jonas — that approach sounds good and keeps risk low. We prefer a per-connection init flag.

We're happy to run the partner integration test on our staging environment; I'll ask our engineering lead to coordinate with Jonas for API shapes. Attaching a cleaned-up diff of our adapter (opsly-sdk-patch.diff) and a short spec doc.

Two additional asks:
1) Can Redwood add a short blurb to your compatibility docs stating that minor version bumps may add optional parameters/hooks but won't change default behavior? Opsly wants that in writing for our security review.
2) If we encounter regressions during partner tests, would Redwood be willing to cut a hotfix branch (patch) outside the default release cadence?

We can be flexible on dates if needed but are aiming to begin partner tests the week of June 29.

Best,
Kai

Attachments: opsly-sdk-patch.diff, opsly-integration-specs.pdf

- On hotfixes: we can commit to a partner hotfix process for integrations running active partner tests (opsly to be listed as a partner with priority hotfix SLA during the test window). We need to align on contact points and acceptable SLAs (48 hours for high severity?).

Next steps:

  2) Aisha: confirm Opsly's preferred contact for hotfix coordination and update the HubSpot deal with the partner test window (week of 2028-06-29).

I'll prepare a short doc for legal review by EOD.

- Vanessa Ortiz
